examples.en: An expert appraised this painting for me.
They appraised the ring at the jewelry shop.
You need a lot of experience to appraise antiques.
The appraised price was higher than I expected.
I'd like to have grandmother's watch appraised.
It takes a week to determine whether it's real.

explain: 물건의 값이나 진짜·가짜를 전문가가 따져 보는 일이에요. 같은 소리의 '감정(feeling)'과는 전혀 달라요. 주로 '감정을 받다', '감정을 맡기다'로 쓰고, 가게에서는 '감정해 주세요'라고 부탁해요.

phrases.en: I took the old watch in and had it appraised.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전문가에게 가치를 확인받는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Having an expert check the value.

phrases.en: Please appraise whether this ring is real.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가게나 전문가에게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking a shop or expert.

phrases.en: I left the appraisal of the painting to an expert.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정할 일을 다른 사람에게 부탁한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means entrusting the appraisal to someone else.

explain_en: An expert determines an object's value or authenticity. It is unrelated to the same-sounding '감정' (feeling). Commonly '감정을 받다' or '감정을 맡기다'; at a shop you ask '감정해 주세요'.

en: to be published; to be run; to be printed

examples.en: My article was published in the newspaper.
I'm waiting for the day my photo appears in the magazine.

examples.ko: 광고가 게재되면 문의 전화가 많이 와요.
examples.en: Once the ad runs, we get lots of calls.
I was happy that my reader's letter got printed.
This article was posted on the website yesterday.
The paper is scheduled to be published in the journal.

explain: 게재되다는 글, 광고, 사진이 신문이나 잡지, 누리집에 실릴 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '실리다'가 더 자연스럽고, 게재되다는 기사나 공지 같은 딱딱한 글에서 많이 나와요. 하는 쪽을 말할 때는 '게재하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The notice was posted on the website.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신문뿐 아니라 인터넷 누리집에 실릴 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for websites as well as newspapers.
phrases.en_equiv: to be posted on the website

phrases.example: 제 글은 다음 달에 게재될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: My article is scheduled to be published next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 실릴 일을 알릴 때 쓰는 자주 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common form for announcing something that will be published.

phrases.en: My photo was printed in a magazine.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '게재되다'보다 '실리다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than '게재되다' in everyday talk.

explain_en: 게재되다 is used when a text, photo or ad appears in a newspaper, magazine or website. In everyday speech Koreans say 실리다 more often; 게재되다 sounds formal and shows up in news and notices. The active partner is 게재하다.

examples.ko: 성적이 나빠서 감독 경질 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: Because the results are bad, there is talk of replacing the manager.

examples.ko: 갑작스러운 경질 소식에 팬들이 많이 놀랐어요.
examples.en: Fans were very surprised by the sudden news of the dismissal.
Calls for the minister to be replaced have grown louder.

examples.ko: 구단은 감독 경질 이유를 아직 밝히지 않았어요.
examples.en: The club hasn't yet revealed why it replaced the manager.

examples.ko: 이번 경질이 팀 분위기를 바꿀 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can this replacement change the team's mood?

examples.ko: 경질 발표가 나자마자 새 후보 이름이 돌았어요.
examples.en: As soon as the dismissal was announced, names of new candidates started going around.

explain: 감독, 장관, 임원처럼 맡은 사람을 그 자리에서 내보내고 다른 사람으로 바꿀 때 써요. 뉴스나 스포츠 기사에서 많이 보이고 '해임'과 비슷하게 쓰여요. '신경질'과는 관계없는 말이니까 헷갈리지 마세요.

phrases.en: Rumors that the coach will be dismissed are worrying the fans.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곧 자리에서 내보낸다는 소문을 말할 때 스포츠 기사에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for rumors that someone will soon be removed; common in sports articles.

phrases.en: The coach was dismissed because of poor results.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내보내는 쪽이 아니라 자리에서 바뀌는 사람을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with the person being replaced as the subject, not the one who dismisses.

phrases.en: News of the president's dismissal came suddenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '경질'과 비슷하게 맡은 일을 그만두게 한다는 뜻인데, 회사나 기관에서 더 넓게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 경질, meaning removing someone from a post, but used more broadly in companies and organizations.

explain_en: It is used when the person holding a post, such as a manager, minister or executive, is removed and replaced by someone else. You see it in news and sports articles, and it is used similarly to '해임' (dismissal). It has nothing to do with '신경질' (irritability), so don't mix them up.

examples.ko: 그 계획은 회사에서 극비로 진행되고 있어요.
examples.en: That plan is being carried out in top secrecy at the company.

examples.ko: 이건 극비 정보니까 아무에게도 말하지 마세요.
examples.en: This is top-secret information, so don't tell anyone.
The president's schedule is top secret for security reasons.

examples.ko: 신제품 출시 날짜는 아직 극비라서 말할 수 없어요.
examples.en: The new product's release date is still top secret, so I can't say.

examples.ko: 극비 문서가 밖으로 새어 나가서 난리가 났어요.
examples.en: A top-secret document leaked out and caused an uproar.

examples.ko: 두 사람은 극비 회담을 마치고 돌아왔어요.
examples.en: The two returned after finishing a top-secret meeting.

explain: '비밀'보다 훨씬 강해서 정부, 군, 회사의 중요한 정보처럼 정말 아무에게도 알리면 안 되는 일에 써요. 친구 사이의 가벼운 비밀은 그냥 '비밀'이라고 해요. '극비 문서', '극비 회담'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 많이 써요.

phrases.en: This top-secret document is kept in a safe.
phrases.nuance_ko: '극비' 뒤에 명사를 붙여 중요한 정보나 자료를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Attach a noun after 극비 to talk about highly sensitive information or materials.

phrases.en: The two companies negotiated in total secrecy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 아무도 모르게 진행될 때 쓰는 부사 꼴로 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adverbial form meaning 'in utmost secrecy', common in news.

phrases.en: Please keep this matter top secret.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 사람에게 절대 알리지 않고 비밀로 하라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking someone to keep something top secret and tell no one.

explain_en: It is much stronger than '비밀' (secret) and is used for truly confidential matters such as government, military or company information. For a light secret between friends, just say '비밀'. It is often placed before a noun, as in '극비 문서' or '극비 회담'.

en: to be planned; to be designed

examples.ko: 이 행사는 여름 방학에 맞춰 기획됐어요.
examples.en: This event was planned to fit the summer break.
A new program is being planned for the students.
It changed a lot from what was first planned.

examples.ko: 그 영화는 십 년 전에 기획되었어요.
examples.en: That movie was planned ten years ago.
It took a long time for the exhibition to be planned.

examples.ko: 새 상품이 기획되는 과정을 보고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to see how a new product gets planned.

explain: '계획'은 앞으로 할 일의 순서를 정하는 것이고, '기획'은 새로운 것을 생각해 내서 짜 놓는 거예요. 영화·방송·전시·상품에 많이 써요. 개인의 하루 일정에는 '계획'을 써요.

phrases.en: The trip was planned a month ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일의 순서를 정한다는 뜻으로 더 널리 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used more broadly for setting up the order of things.

phrases.en: I plan a new exhibition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 직접 짜는 능동형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The active form, where a person designs it.

phrases.example: 이 프로그램은 어린이를 위해 처음 기획됐어요.
phrases.en: This program was first designed for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: '처음'을 붙여 시작 단계를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '처음' points to the starting stage.

explain_en: '계획' is deciding steps for what to do; '기획' is coming up with something new and putting it together. Common for movies, TV, exhibitions and products. For a personal daily schedule, use '계획'.

dis.h: designed as an organized project or event

p.n: 계획 is a general plan; 기획 says it was designed as a project.

examples.ko: 매주 금요일에 팀장님께 진행 상황을 보고해요.
examples.en: Every Friday I report the progress to the team leader.
If there's an accident, report it to the teacher right away.
I reported the results for the second half of the year, from July to December.
I'll report to the manager first and then decide.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 회의 때 사장님께 보고해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to report this problem to the president at the meeting.

examples.ko: 조사 결과를 정리해서 보고하는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a day to organize the survey results and report them.

explain: 회사나 학교에서 윗사람에게 일의 상황이나 결과를 알릴 때 써요. 이럴 때 윗사람에게는 '보고드리다'라고 높여 말해요. '그 뉴스를 보고 놀랐어요'의 '보고'는 '보다'의 활용이라서 전혀 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: I will report the results to you by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 보고할 때 높여서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for reporting to a superior.

phrases.en: I reported yesterday's work to my team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 알린 일을 말할 때 과거형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for something you have already reported.

phrases.en: I have to hand in the report by Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보고한 내용을 적은 글을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The written document with the content you report.

explain_en: It is used at work or school when you tell a superior about the situation or results of something. To a superior, the humble form is '보고드리다'. The '보고' in '그 뉴스를 보고 놀랐어요' is a form of '보다' (to see), so it is a completely different word.

examples.ko: 선생님이 시험 방법을 소상히 설명해 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher explained the exam format in detail.

examples.ko: 사고가 난 경위를 소상히 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: Please tell me in detail how the accident happened.

examples.ko: 계약 내용을 소상히 알고 나서 서명했어요.
examples.en: I signed after learning the contract details thoroughly.

examples.ko: 담당자가 환불 절차를 소상히 안내해 줬어요.
examples.en: The person in charge explained the refund process in detail.

examples.ko: 그 일에 대해서는 제가 소상히 알지 못해요.
examples.en: I don't know the details of that matter.

examples.ko: 여행 일정을 소상히 적어서 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll write out the trip schedule in detail and send it to you.

explain: '자세히'와 뜻은 같지만 더 격식 있고 공식적인 느낌이에요. 편한 대화에서는 '자세히'가 더 자연스러워요. 설명하다, 밝히다, 알리다, 알다 같은 동사와 잘 어울려요.

phrases.example: 어제 있었던 일을 자세히 말해 주세요.
phrases.en: Please tell me in detail what happened yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소상히'와 뜻은 같지만 편한 대화에서 쓰는 가장 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 소상히, but the most natural choice in casual conversation.

phrases.en: The police explained the cause of the incident in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사실을 공식적으로 자세히 알릴 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when officially making facts clear in detail.

phrases.example: 그 일은 제가 소상히 알고 있어요.
phrases.en: I know that matter in detail.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일을 구석구석 잘 알고 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means you know every part of a matter well.

explain_en: It means the same as '자세히' but sounds more formal and official. In casual talk '자세히' feels more natural. It goes well with verbs like 설명하다, 밝히다, 알리다 and 알다.

en: to be collected; to be gathered

examples.en: All the survey results have been collected.

examples.ko: 여러 나라의 우표가 한곳에 수집돼 있어요.
examples.en: Stamps from many countries are collected in one place.
I'll let you know as soon as the data is collected.
The collected data is saved on the computer.
Please explain how the data is collected.
The students' opinions were gathered and taken to the meeting.

explain: '수집되다'는 모으는 사람이 아니라 모이는 자료가 주어예요. 모으는 사람을 말하려면 '수집하다'를 써요. '모이다'는 사람이 모일 때도 쓰지만 '수집되다'는 사람에게 쓰지 않고, 자료·정보·의견과 같이 써요.

phrases.en: The students' opinions have not been collected yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자료나 의견이 아직 모이지 않았다는 부정 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a negative form saying data or opinions have not been gathered yet.

phrases.en: In this app, user information is collected.
phrases.nuance_ko: '정보', '자료', '의견'처럼 모이는 것이 주어로 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The subject is what is gathered, like information, data, or opinions.

phrases.en: A lot of the necessary data has been gathered.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수집되다'보다 쉽고 일상적이에요. 사람에게도 쓸 수 있어서 뜻이 더 넓어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is simpler and more everyday than '수집되다'. It also works for people, so it is broader.

explain_en: With '수집되다' the subject is the material being gathered, not the person gathering; use '수집하다' for the collector. '모이다' can be used when people gather, but '수집되다' is not used for people and goes with data, information, and opinions.

examples.ko: 새 프로젝트가 순항 중이라서 마음이 놓여요.
examples.en: The new project is going smoothly, so I feel relieved.

examples.ko: 올해 첫 달은 매출이 순항으로 시작했어요.
examples.en: This year began smoothly, with sales going well in the first month.

examples.ko: 비행기가 순항 고도에 오르면 안내 방송이 나와요.
examples.en: When the plane reaches cruising altitude, an announcement is made.

examples.ko: 이 배는 파도 없이 조용히 순항을 이어 갔어요.
examples.en: This ship kept on cruising quietly without any waves.
You shouldn't be satisfied with the smooth start.

examples.ko: 회사의 순항 덕분에 연말 보너스도 기대돼요.
examples.en: Thanks to the company's smooth run, I'm looking forward to a year-end bonus.

explain: 배나 비행기가 안정적으로 가는 것에서 나와, 일이 문제없이 잘 풀리는 것을 비유할 때 자주 써요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '난항'이에요. 보통 '순항 중'이라는 꼴로 많이 들어요.

phrases.en: The construction is going smoothly, so there is nothing to worry about.
phrases.nuance_ko: '순항'이 일이 잘 풀리는 상태를 말한다면 '순항 중'은 지금 그렇게 진행되고 있다는 뜻이라서 가장 흔하게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '순항' names smooth progress, while '순항 중' says things are going that way right now, which is the most common form.

phrases.example: 우리 팀은 올해도 순항을 이어 가고 있어요.
phrases.en: Our team is keeping up its smooth run this year too.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 번의 순항이 아니라 좋은 흐름이 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the good run continues, not just a single smooth moment.

phrases.en: This project is expected to go smoothly from the start.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 일이 잘 풀릴 것 같다는 전망을 말할 때 쓰는 뉴스 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase for predicting that things will go well.

explain_en: It comes from ships and planes moving steadily, and is often used figuratively for work going well without trouble. The word with the opposite feel is '난항'. You hear it most often in the form '순항 중'.

examples.en: The mayor inspected the newly built park.
The minister inspected the factory and encouraged the employees.
A delegation is scheduled to inspect the school tomorrow.

examples.ko: 직접 시찰해 보니 문제가 훨씬 심각했어요.
examples.en: After inspecting it in person, the problem was much more serious.

examples.ko: 해외 시설을 시찰하러 다음 주에 출장을 가요.
examples.en: I'm going on a business trip next week to inspect overseas facilities.

examples.ko: 시찰하는 동안에는 사진을 찍으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not take photos while the inspection is going on.

explain: '점검하다', '둘러보다'와 달리 윗사람이나 대표가 현장을 직접 보러 간다는 느낌이 있어요. '공장을 시찰하다'처럼 목적어는 장소가 오고, 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 뉴스나 공식적인 글에서 많이 봐요.

phrases.en: The CEO personally inspected the construction site.
phrases.nuance_ko: 장소를 직접 살펴본다는 뜻의 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic pairing for inspecting a place in person.

phrases.en: The minister will go to inspect the school tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-(으)러 가다'를 붙여 목적을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -(으)러 가다 states the purpose of going.

phrases.en: The chairman inspected the new factory yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람의 행동이라 존댓말로 쓰는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form, since the actor is usually a high-status person.

explain_en: Unlike '점검하다' or '둘러보다', it carries the feel of a superior or representative going to see a site in person. The object is a place, as in '공장을 시찰하다', and it is rare in casual talk but common in the news and formal writing.

examples.en: This factory mass produces electric cars.
We plan to start mass producing the new model next year.
The prototype succeeded, but we haven't been able to mass produce it yet.
To bring the price down, the parts have to be mass produced.

examples.ko: 회사는 휴대폰을 양산한 뒤 해외로 보냈어요.
examples.en: The company mass produced the phones and then shipped them overseas.

examples.ko: 이 기계로 하루에 천 개를 양산하고 있어요.
examples.en: We are turning out a thousand a day with this machine.

explain: 공장에서 같은 물건을 많이 만들 때 써요. 시제품을 처음 만드는 일은 '제작하다'라고 하고, 시장에 내놓을 만큼 본격적으로 만들 때 양산이라고 해요. 안 좋은 것이 계속 생길 때도 '문제를 양산하다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: keep producing problems
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋지 않은 것이 계속 많이 생겨날 때 비유로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for when unwanted things keep appearing in large numbers.

explain_en: Use it when a factory makes lots of the same product. Making a first prototype is '제작하다', and 양산 is making it in earnest, enough to sell. It is also used when bad things keep coming out, as in '문제를 양산하다'.

en: to be satisfactory; to be fine; to be favorable

examples.en: The patient's condition is better than yesterday.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 공기 질이 대체로 양호해요.
examples.en: The air quality in this area is generally good.
The test results were good.
I heard the company's finances are in good shape.
If the weather is good, we will leave tomorrow.
I graduated with good grades.

explain: '양호하다'는 보고서, 뉴스, 건강검진처럼 격식 있는 글과 말에서 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '괜찮다', '좋다'를 훨씬 많이 말해요. 문제없이 괜찮은 정도라서 '아주 좋다'와는 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: My eyesight is fairly good.
phrases.nuance_ko: '편'이 들어가서 대체로 괜찮다는 부드러운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word '편' gives a softer sense of being generally fine.
phrases.en_equiv: to be on the good side

phrases.en: The patient's condition is still not good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상태가 괜찮지 않다고 격식 있게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal way to say that a condition is not fine.

phrases.en: My condition is fine today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '양호하다'보다 훨씬 자연스럽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Much more natural than 양호하다 in everyday conversation.

explain_en: '양호하다' belongs to reports, news and medical or checkup results. In everyday talk people say '괜찮다' or '좋다'. It means fine, with no problems, which is weaker than 'very good'.

en: to be completed; to come to a full end (series, work)

examples.en: That webtoon ended last year.
There is still a long way to go before the story is finished.

examples.ko: 시리즈가 완결돼서 한꺼번에 읽을 수 있어요.
examples.en: The series has ended, so you can read it all at once.
I tend to pick and watch only finished works.

examples.ko: 드라마가 완결되면 팬 모임을 열 거예요.
examples.en: When the drama wraps up, we will hold a fan meeting.
This novel ends in three volumes.

explain: '끝나다'는 아무 일에나 쓰지만 '완결되다'는 소설, 만화, 웹툰, 시리즈처럼 이야기가 끝까지 마무리될 때 주로 써요. 반대말은 '연재되다'(아직 계속 나오는 중)예요. 일을 마친다는 말로는 잘 안 써요.

phrases.en: I read the completed webtoon all at once.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이야기가 끝까지 다 나온 작품 앞에 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a work whose story is fully finished.

phrases.en: This novel is not finished yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 이야기가 계속 나오는 중일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the story is still ongoing.

phrases.en: That drama ended yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완결되다'와 달리 어떤 일에도 쓸 수 있는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike '완결되다', this easy word works for any kind of event.

explain_en: '끝나다' works for almost anything, but 완결되다 is mostly used when a story such as a novel, comic, webtoon, or series reaches its proper ending. The opposite is '연재되다' (still being released). It is not used for finishing everyday tasks.

en: to appoint; to nominate; to designate

examples.en: The president appoints Manager Kim as team leader.
The president appointed a new minister.

examples.ko: 학교는 그를 새 교장으로 임명하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The school decided to appoint him as the new principal.
It's a company where the chairman personally appoints the head.

examples.ko: 사람을 임명하면 그에게 권한도 함께 줘야 해요.
examples.en: When you appoint a person, you also have to give them authority.

examples.ko: 새 대표를 임명할 때는 직원들의 의견도 들어요.
examples.en: When appointing a new head, we also hear the staff's opinions.

explain: 위에서 사람을 골라 자리를 맡길 때 써요. 같은 상황에서 '뽑다'는 여러 사람 중에서 고르는 일상적인 말이고, '임명하다'는 공식적이고 권한이 있는 사람이 정해요. 반대로 그만두게 하면 '해임하다'예요.

phrases.en: The president chose Minsu as team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: '임명하다'보다 일상적이고 여러 사람 중에서 골라 맡긴다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More everyday than 임명하다, with the sense of picking someone from among many.

phrases.en: The company decided to appoint him as team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 임명하겠다고 결정했을 때 쓰는 모양이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when it has been decided to appoint someone.

phrases.en: The president entrusted him with the team leader post.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이나 자리를 다른 사람에게 주어 책임지게 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when giving someone a job or post to be responsible for.

explain_en: Used when someone above chooses a person and gives them a position. 뽑다 is the everyday word for picking from many people, while 임명하다 is formal and done by someone with authority. Removing someone from the post is 해임하다.

examples.en: I check the car before departing.

examples.ko: 건물 관리인이 매달 소방 시설을 점검했어요.
examples.en: The building manager inspected the fire equipment every month.

examples.ko: 시험이 끝나기 전에 답안을 한 번 더 점검할 거예요.
examples.en: I will check my answers once more before the exam ends.
They are inspecting the elevator right now.
After checking, if there is no problem, we start.
Please write the inspection record here.

explain: 기계·시설·계획이 문제없는지 하나씩 살필 때 써요. '확인하다'보다 하나씩 꼼꼼히 살피는 느낌이 있어요. 명사 '점검'은 '정기 점검'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 엘리베이터는 한 달에 한 번 정기 점검을 해요.
phrases.en: The elevator gets a regular inspection once a month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 정해진 때마다 하는 검사를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for checks done at set times.

phrases.en: The school did a safety check today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위험한 곳이 없는지 살펴볼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when checking for anything dangerous.

phrases.example: 발표 전에 내용을 한번 점검해 보세요.
phrases.en: Check your content once before the presentation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한번 시도하듯 살펴보라고 부드럽게 권할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A soft suggestion to give something a check.

explain_en: Use it when you go through a machine, facility, or plan item by item to see if anything is wrong. It feels more thorough than '확인하다'. The noun 점검 appears in '정기 점검' (regular inspection).

examples.ko: 내일 오전에 팀장님께 중간보고를 해야 해요.
examples.en: I have to give the team leader an interim report tomorrow morning.
Have you finished making the materials for the interim report?
Many problems came up in the interim report.
The project's interim report is next Friday.

examples.ko: 중간보고는 짧게 핵심만 말하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For an interim report, it's best to say only the key points briefly.
I haven't even given an interim report and the deadline is already here.

explain: 일이 끝나기 전에 진행 상황을 알리는 거라서 끝난 뒤의 '최종 보고'와 짝으로 써요. '중간보고를 하다'라고 하고, 윗사람에게는 '중간보고를 드리다'라고 해요. '중간 보고'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.

phrases.en: I'll give an interim report on Friday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 진행 상황을 알리는 가장 기본 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say you report on progress.

phrases.en: I gave an interim report to the team leader.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람에게 보고할 때 높여서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The honorific form for reporting to a superior.

phrases.en: After the interim report comes the final report.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 끝난 뒤의 보고로, '중간보고'와 짝이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The report after the work is finished; pairs with 중간보고.

explain_en: It reports progress before the work is done, so it pairs with '최종 보고' (final report). You say '중간보고를 하다', and '중간보고를 드리다' to a superior. It is sometimes written with a space as '중간 보고'.
